stories.title: 'Lover converted to Islam to usurp property worth crores':Victim's father claims, 'Gym trainer trapped him and organised fake nikah'
stories.summary: 'My 27-year-old son was trapped in a love trap by gym trainer Chandni Qureshi. Then she converted his religion from Hindu to Muslim. Later, she performed a fake nikah (marriage).' This is the statement of Devraj Singh, a millionaire medicine businessman from Shamli. He said, " My son had According to the police, Chandni and Ayush Malik met in 2022. Both met at a physiotherapy centre. There, they exchanged each other's numbers and their conversations began. Within a few days, both joined the gym "Qureshi Plus". There, they used to meet daily. Their affair started from there. Chandni belongs to a very poor family. Her father runs a juice cart. Her siblings work in a mall. Chandni used to pretend to be rich. After befriending Ayush, Chandni would take money from him. She bought a gold chain with Ayush's money. She also made Ayush spend a lot more money. Chandni, along with her entire family, brainwashed Ayush. She asked him to become Muslim. After this, Ayush separated from his family. He left Hinduism and adopted Muslim customs and practices. Ayush separated from home 6 months after nikah Chandni and her family took Ayush to Delhi. There, they converted his religion. Then Chandni got married (nikah) there itself. Ayush's family members did not know anything about the nikah. Just 6 months after the nikah, Ayush separated from his family. He rented a house in the city area. Both of them started living there together. Ayush's father alleges that when we started opposing these things, Chandni's family also pressured us to change our religion. They also threatened to kill us. Chandni's brother, Aman Qureshi, used to work at Devraj Singh's shop. He taught Ayush everything about Islam. Father said - My son is very simple. Strict action should be taken against the accused Ayush's father, Devraj Singh Malik, says," We follow the Hindu religion. Puja is performed twice a day at home. I myself go to the temple twice a day. These people lured and deceived my son and converted his religion. My son is very simple. Strict action should be taken against all of them. These people have taken lakhs of rupees from my son''. SP says, 'Chandni's family wanted to usurp property' SP NP Singh says, investigation has revealed that a Muslim leader from Pakistan who carries out religious conversions, his page was made to be followed by Ayush. Chandni's younger brother had done this. A case has been registered against 10 people. Chandni Qureshi and her father, Islam, have been arrested. 8 others are still absconding. The role of a local doctor, Khurshid Anwar, is also being investigated in the case. Chandni and her family wanted to grab property worth billions of rupees. Police are now investigating every angle. Ayush had done B Pharma, Chandni is a physiotherapist Ayush Malik has three sisters. They are married. And, now parents are left at home. Ayush Malik's father, Devraj Singh Malik, has a big name among medicine traders. Ayush has done B Pharma. Chandni Qureshi has four sisters and two brothers. Parents are left at home. Chandni has done a physiotherapist course after passing 12th with Arts.

stories.title: UP police aspirant breaks down after exam:Candidates say maths section was tricky; 2.8 lakh competing for 32,000 posts
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Police constable recruitment examination for 32,679 posts was held today (Monday). The second shift began at 3 pm and concluded at 5 pm. Candidates were allowed into exam halls only after stringent checks, including admit card verification, biometric matching, and retina scans. Security measures varied across districts. In Jhansi, candidates were asked to remove their shoes and socks. In Saharanpur, gold chains and spectacles were removed for inspection. In Jaunpur, women candidates were asked to open their hair buns for checking, while in Kanpur, candidates with long hair or beards underwent additional screening. In Mainpuri, a woman candidate broke down after the exam, alleging that her OMR sheet was taken away eight minutes before the test ended. More than 2.8 lakh candidates are expected to appear for the examination over three days, June 8, 9, and 10. The exam is being conducted across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh at 1,183 centres. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced a 50% fare concession for candidates travelling on state-run buses upon showing their admit cards. See pictures Know about constable recruitment

stories.title: Weather changes in UP, heavy rainfall lashes Jalaun:Rain alert for Lucknow in next 3 hrs; winds expected to gust up to 70 kmph
stories.summary: The spell of thunderstorms and rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. Most districts began Monday with bright sunshine, while reduced wind speeds led to humid conditions. However, by around 10 am, the weather changed, with clouds covering districts including Lucknow, Barabanki and Hardoi, accompanied by cool winds. Earlier in the morning, Jalaun received heavy rainfall at around 8:30 am, providing relief from the heat. Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for Lucknow, warning of thunderstorms, lightning, and rain over the next three hours. The alert, sent to mobile phones, predicts moderate rainfall and strong winds, with gusts reaching up to 70 kmph. According to IMD, this time monsoon may reach UP 4 to 6 days late. The pre-monsoon rain spell will start after June 11. Monsoon may enter the state by June 24. Then, within 10 days, it will cover the entire UP. Monsoon usually reaches UP between June 18 and 20. Talking about the last 24 hours, the maximum temperature in 12 districts of the state remained at 40 °C or above. Banda-Jhansi were the hottest cities, where the maximum temperature was recorded at 43.2 °C. Due to the scorching sun, it became difficult for people to step out of their homes. The effect of heat was also seen on animals. At Kanpur Zoo, a tigress sat in the water pool for hours, enjoying herself. The tiger was bathed with a pipe. Water sprinklers or fountains were arranged for the deer. Most animals were seen sitting in the shade throughout the day. Lucknow's meteorological scientist, Atul Singh, said- Pre-monsoon rains have not started yet. That's why it's hot. Heatwave conditions are developing. Pre-monsoon rains may start in 3-4 days. This will bring down the temperature. Along with relief from heat, a new spell of rain will begin.A tiger resting in the shade of a tree amidst intense heat at Kanpur Zoo. stories.title: SBSP finalises contenders for 44 seats:Stakes claim to 8 BJP seats; OP Rajbhar raises pressure on 5 constituencies
stories.summary: Amidst discussions of the UP assembly elections being held earlier than scheduled, political parties have started their preparations. Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), which contested 19 seats with the SP last time, is preparing to contest 44 seats in 2027. Among these, 8 currently have BJP MLAs. There are 2 seats where Nishad Party candidates contested last time. OP Rajbhar has also finalized candidates for Ghosi, the seat of UP government minister Dara Singh Chauhan, and Madhuban, the seat of Energy Minister AK Sharma. 5 Prominent Seats Claimed by SBSP Ghosi- On this seat in Mau district, Dara Singh Chauhan of SP won by 22 thousand votes in 2022. Later, he resigned and contested the by-election from BJP, but lost to Sudhakar Singh of SP. Sudhakar Singh has also passed away. Suheldev Bhartiya Samaj Party (SBSP) has appointed State Vice President Phagu Singh as in-charge and National Spokesperson of Yuva Manch Jitendra Kumar Bharti as co-in-charge for this seat. Madhuban- Currently, BJP's Ramvilas Chauhan is the MLA from this assembly seat in Mau district. Energy Minister AK Sharma has an eye on this seat. SBSP has appointed National Vice President Dr. Santosh Pandey as in-charge and State President of Labor Cell Ritesh Mall as co-in-charge. Itwa- Currently, Leader of Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey holds this seat in Siddharthnagar district. In 2022, he defeated Satish Chandra Dwivedi, who was the Basic Education Minister, by 1662 votes on this seat. SBSP has appointed Purvanchal State Vice President Keshav Rajbhar as in-charge and District President Siddharthnagar Ramniwas Rajbhar as co-in-charge. Malhani- On this Jaunpur seat, SP's Lucky Yadav is currently the MLA. In 2022, he defeated JDU candidate Dhananjay Singh by a margin of over 17,000 votes. This time too, Dhananjay Singh is preparing to contest the election from here. He is strengthening ties with Suhaspa. Suhaspa has appointed Brijbhan Rajbhar as in-charge. Isauli- SP's Mohammad Tahir Khan won this seat in Sultanpur district by defeating BJP's Omprakash Pandey by 269 votes. Suhaspa has appointed party's senior leader Shivkumar Singh as in-charge and district organisation minister Manoj Sharma as co-in-charge. SBSP's focus is on strengthening the organisation in these districts Subhaspa is eyeing Ghazipur, Jaunpur, Varanasi, Chandauli, Bhadohi, Azamgarh, Mau, Ballia, Deoria, Kushinagar, and Maharajganj in Purvanchal. Meanwhile, it is also focusing on Ambedkar Nagar, Sultanpur, Siddharthnagar, Basti, and Barabanki in the Awadh region. Subhaspa is also looking at Hardoi and Sitapur in Central UP, and Banda in Bundelkhand. Additionally, it has its eyes on districts like Shamli, Bijnor, Moradabad, and Firozabad in Western UP. Om Prakash Rajbhar is busy strengthening his party in these districts by mobilising Rajbhars and the extremely backward classes. Strategy formulated in the national council meeting Subhaspa's National Council meeting was held recently in Varanasi. In the organisational meeting, held in the presence of National President Om Prakash Rajbhar and National Principal General Secretary Dr. Arvind Rajbhar, it was decided that before the 2027 assembly elections, the party should prepare strongly for at least 50 to 60 seats in the state. BJP-held seats on which SBSP has staked a claim ahead of seat-sharing talks In these assembly constituencies, an agreement has been reached to strengthen the organisation up to the booth level. For this, a target has been set to connect the deprived and extremely backward castes with the party. Nishad Party contested 2 seats, RLD's won 1 seat also under scrutiny OP Rajbhar, disregarding the coalition equations, has also fielded his candidates on these seats of the allies. Nishad Party (2 seats) : On the Atrauliya seat of Azamgarh, OP Rajbhar has already held a large public meeting after appointing his son Arun Rajbhar as in-charge. Here in 2022, Nishad Party's Prashant Singh lost to SP's Sangram Yadav by 17 thousand votes. SBSP has fielded Kaluram Prajapati on the Kalpi seat of Jalaun. Here, the Nishad Party had lost by 2,816 votes. RLD (1 seat) : On Shamli's Thana Bhawan seat, which was won by RLD's Ashraf Ali Khan in 2022, SBSP has appointed Pawan Kashyap as in-charge. SBSP's 5 'strongholds', where Rajbhar himself is in charge SBSP's eye on these 19 seats won by SP Subhaspa has deployed in-charges to strengthen its hold among the extremely backward and Rajbhar voters in areas influenced by SP. Jaunpur-Ballia-Chandauli- Kerakat (Ritesh Ram), Rasra (Shivendra Singh), Sakaldiha (Nityanand Pandey), Sikanderpur (Rajnish Srivastava), Phephna (Ajay Rajbhar). Azamgarh and Ambedkar Nagar- Bhadohi Sadar (Rakesh Verma), Phulpur Pawai (Khursheed Alam), Didarganj (Shailendra Singh), Azamgarh Sadar (Hemant Singh), Mehnagar (Ramdahin Paswan), Mohammadabad Gohna (Santosh Master), Akbarpur (Vichelal Rajbhar-MLC), Jalalpur (Ramtesh Dubey), Tanda (Radhika Patel). Other Districts. Rudhauli (Basti- Ramlalit Chaudhary), Moradabad Rural (Ravi Chaudhary), Shikohabad (Firozabad- Shishupal Yadav), Baberu (Banda- Lallu Singh Khangar), Najibabad (Bijnor- Mo. Shahabuddin). BJP also claimed these seats which it narrowly missed Isauli- On this seat in Sultanpur district, Shivkumar Singh, Senior Leader (In-charge), Manoj Sharma, District Organisation Minister Sultanpur (Co-in-charge). BJP lost to SP's Mohammad Tahir by just 269 votes. Dumariyaganj- On this seat in Siddharthnagar district, Ganga Ram Rajbhar, State Vice President (In-charge), Amjad Khan, Senior Leader (Co-in-charge). SP's Sayyada Khatoon won against BJP by a margin of just 771 votes. Basti Sadar- Vinod Rajbhar, National Secretary (In-charge), Brijbhushan Mishra, State President Intellectual Cell (Co-in-charge). SP's Mahendra Nath Yadav defeated BJP's Dayaram Chaudhary by 1779 votes. Pharenda- On this seat in Maharajganj district, Jitendra Singh, National Secretary (In-charge), Kabilash Rajbhar, State Vice President (Co-in-charge). Congress's Virendra Chaudhary won against BJP's Bajrang Bahadur Singh by just 1246 votes. Ramnagar- On this seat in Barabanki district, Sanjay Tiwari is the National Secretary (In-charge), and Anil Rajbhar is the State Secretary Madhyanchal (Co-in-charge). SP's Farid Mahfooz Kidwai had defeated BJP by 261 votes.

stories.title: 4 UP MPs fall ill during Ladakh tour:Lalganj MP vomits blood; admitted to AIIMS; Afzal Ansari put on oxygen support
stories.summary: 4 MPs from UP fell ill in Leh-Ladakh. Due to lack of oxygen at high altitude, the MPs experienced severe difficulty in breathing. One MP had to be admitted to Delhi AIIMS after vomiting blood from the nose and mouth. Meanwhile, other MPs had to remain on oxygen support from the car to the hotel. This tour started on May 16, 2026, led by DMK Rajya Sabha MP from Tamil Nadu, Tiruchi Siva. This team of 17 MPs included 4 MPs from UP. These MPs were part of the Leh-Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir tour of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry. Health deteriorated at an altitude of 12 to 14 thousand feet The committee members reached Leh, located at an altitude of about 12,500 feet above ground, on May 19. The very next day, the team went to see the saltwater Pangong Lake, situated at an altitude of 14,588 feet. Due to the sudden ascent to such a high altitude, the oxygen levels of most MPs and their family members dropped rapidly. In the entire convoy, only 2-3 MPs did not require oxygen. The rest all fell ill. UP MP said - It's difficult to breathe there He said- It's a mistake by those who planned the tour; no rest was given MP Afzal Ansari says- My oxygen level dropped to 37, whereas it should be 91 to 100. There was a mistake by those who planned the tour. Upon reaching Leh, 48 to 72 hours of rest was necessary, which was not given. I had to stay on oxygen support from the car to the hotel. The oxygen cylinder remained with me. In Ladakh, zero or sub-zero temperatures and the lack of trees make life very difficult. 'Blood started flowing from my mouth and nose' MP Daroga Prasad Saroj said- As soon as I reached a high altitude in Ladakh, I started having difficulty breathing. Soon, blood started coming from my mouth and nose. Oxygen support was immediately provided. After returning from the 7-day tour, I had to be admitted to Delhi AIIMS, where my treatment is still ongoing under the supervision of doctors. Life there is extremely difficult. The salary of our soldiers protecting the country should not be less than 10 lakh rupees. Doctors' team with us, got treatment MP Rakesh Rathore says- The problem of oxygen always persists in Leh-Ladakh. Local people are accustomed to it, but it is natural for outsiders to face problems. The relief was that a complete team of doctors was present with the parliamentary committee, due to which everyone immediately received medical help. MP Chandan Chauhan from Bijnor seat in UP also went to Leh-Ladakh. His health also deteriorated due to a lack of oxygen. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact him, but his phone was not answered. Afzal met arch-rival Manoj Sinha after 30 years During this visit, an interesting political incident also came to light. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha welcomed the parliamentary committee at Raj Bhavan in Jammu. In Ghazipur politics, Manoj Sinha and Afzal Ansari have had a long-standing and deep political rivalry. This was the first meeting between the two leaders since 1996. Afzal Ansari said - Manoj Sinha ji welcomed me with great warmth and respect. Political differences are one thing, but his behaviour touched my heart. After the meeting, LG Sinha presented me with Mata Vaishno Devi's prasad, a traditional Kashmiri shawl, and saffron. Visited Pulwama and Pahalgam Members of the committee also visited those sensitive places where terrorist attacks had occurred. The team visited the site of the 2019 Pulwama attack and the site of the Pahalgam incident that took place last April. How Pashmina shawls are made, this was also learned. During the visit, MPs understood the intricacies of Kashmir's famous Pashmina shawl. Afzal Ansari stated that this world-famous shawl is made from the wool of special cows and sheep living in the high mountains of Ladakh, the price of which can be up to ₹5 lakh. During the Leh visit, various ongoing development projects there and their progress were also reviewed by the State Bank of India (SBI).

stories.title: 27,000 names deleted from Panchayat election list:3rd phase verification completed, final list to be published on 10th
stories.summary: In the three-tier panchayat elections, around 27,000 names are being deleted from the voter list after the completion of the third phase of verification of suspected duplicate voters. Month-long verification drive completed During nearly a month-long verification exercise, officials found around 27,000 individuals whose names appeared not only in their respective gram panchayats but also in two or more other gram panchayats within the district. A consolidated list has been prepared, and these names are now being removed. The final voter list will be published on 10 June. Special revision and voter count changes Along with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the voter list for panchayat elections was also revised. The draft list published earlier had a total of 29.88 lakh voters, while after SIR the number rose to around 31 lakh. This led to a situation where the number of voters in gram panchayats and the overall district (including urban local bodies) appeared nearly equal, raising administrative concerns. Large-scale duplication checks conducted Since SIR data could not be questioned, the panchayat voter list was re-examined. Initially, BLO-level scrutiny identified around 30,000 duplicate entries. The State Election Commission then sent a list of 5.16 lakh suspected duplicate voters, prepared at block level. BLOs were instructed to enter the last four digits of Aadhaar numbers for verification. After this process, 1.51 lakh voters were found to be duplicate, bringing the total identified duplicates in the first round to about 1.81 lakh. However, due to the addition of nearly 2 lakh new voters, the final list remained largely unaffected. Second large list sent for verification Later, the State Election Commission sent another list containing 12.37 lakh suspected duplicate voters, this time prepared at district level. After Aadhaar-based verification through BLOs, 1.27 lakh duplicate voters were identified and removed from the list. Third list still under verification When officials believed the process was complete, another list surfaced containing 11.33 lakh suspected duplicate entries, also prepared at district level. So far, 62% of this verification has been completed, and around 14,000 duplicate voters have been identified in this phase.

stories.title: 1.33-lakh to appear for police recruitment exam at 50 centres:3-day test in six shifts, police and STF to monitor
stories.summary: The administration in Varanasi has completed preparations for the three-day UP Police recruitment examination scheduled from 8 to 10 June. A total of 1.32 lakh candidates will appear in the exam, which will be conducted at 50 schools designated as examination centres. Exam to be held in six shifts The examination will be conducted in two shifts per day, making it a total of six shifts across three days. The first shift will be held from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon, while the second shift will take place from 3:00 pm to 5:00 pm. At each of the 50 centres, 22,032 candidates will appear in every shift. A large number of security personnel will be deployed at the examination centres. Police, STF, LIU, intelligence units, and several other agencies will also monitor the examination process. High-level coordination meeting held A joint coordination meeting was held at the Police Lines auditorium to ensure a smooth and transparent conduct of the examination. Officials discussed preparations in line with government directives.The District Magistrate informed that all arrangements have been completed for the exam scheduled from 8 to 10 June. He also stressed the need for inter-departmental coordination given the large scale and sensitivity of the examination. Focus on law, order and logistics Discussions were held on maintaining law and order and smooth traffic management during the examination days. Key areas reviewed included security arrangements, smooth entry and exit of candidates, crowd management around centres, traffic and parking arrangements, public facilities, electricity and water supply, sanitation, and emergency services. Arrangements were also discussed for railway stations, bus stands, major intersections, and areas surrounding examination centres. Officials present in meeting The meeting was attended by Additional CP Shivhari Meena, District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar, SP (EOW) Pradeep Kumar, Additional Commissioner Alok Kumar Verma, ADCP Namrata Srivastava, ADM Rajesh Kumar and Govind Singh, DIOS Bholendra Pratap Singh, along with other departmental officials, zonal and sector magistrates, police officers, and examination centre in-charges.

stories.title: Dimple Yadav bows before Shankaracharya, seeks apology:Says SP chief stands with him; nature will avenge the insult
stories.summary: Badri Nath Jyotish Peeth Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand reached Mainpuri on Friday with his “cow protection yatra”. Here, Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav met him. She bowed before him, sought his blessings, and also presented him a shawl. After this, Dimple sat on the ground with folded hands in front of the Shankaracharya. He reiterated his demand to declare the cow as “Rashtra Mata” (Mother of the Nation). Dimple Yadav expressed regret over the Kannauj incident and said the Shankaracharya had to spend a night on the road, adding that the party felt sorry for it. Dimple also said that SP national president Akhilesh Yadav fully supports the Shankaracharya’s campaign and will continue to do so in the future. She further remarked that the disrespect shown to the Shankaracharya during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj would be “answered by nature itself”. See 2 pictures... SP MP pays respects at the event Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand was staying at the marriage hall of former SP MLA Rajkumar Yadav in Mainpuri. He mentioned the incident in Kannauj where he had to spend the night on the roadside. Dimple Yadav told him that Akhilesh Yadav was deeply hurt over the incident, adding that if he had known earlier, proper arrangements would have been made. She also said Akhilesh had apologised to him. The Shankaracharya responded that since it was not Dimple’s fault, there was no need for an apology, but he appreciated the sensitivity shown. After about an hour-long programme, he left for Kishani. “Insult to Sanatan Dharma being witnessed” Dimple Yadav said the Shankaracharya deserved full respect and expressed concern over what she called disrespect towards Sanatan Dharma, adding that the world was witnessing it. She also criticised those in power, saying people were seeing how religious leaders were being disrespected. She compared the stature of Shankaracharyas to the four Vedas and said their dignity was very significant. Dimple added that such disrespect would be answered by nature. She reiterated that Akhilesh Yadav and the Samajwadi Party stood firmly with the Shankaracharya and his movement. Shankaracharya vows to continue movement Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand said his primary resolve is to secure constitutional recognition for declaring the cow as “Mother of the Nation”. He said the movement would continue until the demand is fulfilled. Allegations of administrative pressure Earlier on 3 June, during his yatra in Kannauj, arrangements for his night stay at a private school in Chhibramau were cancelled after alleged administrative intervention. Organisers claimed permission was withdrawn at the last moment. After this, the Shankaracharya stayed at a temporary tent set up at a roadside venue, where police remained deployed overnight. Supporters alleged lack of basic facilities like electricity and fans. He later accused the administration of harassment, saying he was forced to stay on government land after being denied accommodation. Akhilesh met Shankaracharya three months ago SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had met Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand in Lucknow on 12 March. The meeting lasted about an hour, during which Akhilesh was seen sitting on the floor before him. After the meeting, Akhilesh told the media that he had met the Shankaracharya with respect and added that “fake saints would now be exposed”. Cow protection campaign The Shankaracharya had launched his cow protection campaign from Varanasi. His journey covered several districts including Jaunpur, Sultanpur, Sitapur, and Lucknow as part of a wider outreach movement.

stories.title: Murder, loot planned on WhatsApp groups:Limbs broken for ₹500; ‘Katra Gang’ kills hotel businessman’s son
stories.summary: On the night of 29 May, in Ghazipur, the son of hotel businessman Vineet Rai was shot dead. The murder was allegedly planned on a WhatsApp group named “Katra Gang”. Everything—from how many bullets would be fired, which weapon would be used, and how the killing would be carried out—was decided in advance. This is not the first such case in Uttar Pradesh. In districts like Maharajganj, Ballia and Unnao, criminals are increasingly using WhatsApp groups to plan crimes. Whether it is extortion, assault or murder, the planning is often done on these groups. These networks have now become a major challenge for the administration. Read the report… Four members of the “Katra Gang” opened multiple rounds of firing on Vineet Rai. He was hit by four bullets and later died in hospital. Accused called himself “King of Ghazipur” In Ghazipur, Alok Rai runs a luxury hotel worth around ₹20 crore. His son Vineet used to manage the business. On 29 May, around 11 pm, four masked men arrived on two bikes. They first spoke to the guard Shambhu outside and asked for 16 bottles of beer. He told them it was available. They took 8 bottles. At that moment, Vineet came out to go home and walked towards his vehicle. As he reached his car, the attackers opened fire. The first bullet hit his hand, and he tried to run. The second hit his waist and he fell down. After that, two more bullets were fired into his chest. He was taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The four accused—Shankar Pandey, Kamlesh Chaudhary, Sonu Yadav and Monu Tripathi—are absconding. Shankar Pandey is the main accused. Shankar Pandey used to upload “dreaded gangster-style” videos on YouTube. People used to comment asking him to add them to his WhatsApp group. ₹1 crore extortion demand led to murder According to Vineet’s father Alok Rai, the accused had been threatening him for the past two years and demanding extortion money. They called it “gang tax” and demanded ₹1 crore, saying the hotel was worth ₹20 crore. They had also vandalised the hotel several times. Police investigation has revealed that Shankar Pandey had formed a gang called “Katra Gang” and created a WhatsApp group with members involved in criminal activity. They projected themselves on social media as the “King of Ghazipur” and Shankar called himself a “Bahubali”. According to the family, the gang was involved in several crimes over the past two years: “Contract killing for ₹500” in Ballia In neighbouring Ballia district, youths in the Beltharoad area (PIN 221715) formed a gang and created a WhatsApp group. Inside the group, discussions reportedly included committing violent acts such as breaking someone’s arms or legs for just ₹500. The group grew to more than 70 members and carried out crimes including assault and robbery. Some members allegedly received political protection. Later, the group split into two factions. In October 2025, a dispute broke out and a young man named Ayush was shot dead. Police registered cases against four accused: Robin Singh, Pawan Singh, Rohit and Raj. Even after six months, no one associated with the group is openly active now. 28 arrested after gang clash In the Gorakhpur–Maharajganj border area, gangs named “AK-47 Gang” and “Red Gang” emerged last year. They used WhatsApp groups to organise assaults, threats and extortion. Some members even used bikes with “AK-47” written on them and gun symbols. On 27 October 2025, both groups clashed violently, leading to stone-pelting and firing. Six people were seriously injured. Police arrested 28 people, including several minors. Some were paraded in public after arrest. Young boys aged 18–22 involved in crime During the COVID period, groups like “Mahakal” and “Gunda” were formed in Gorakhpur. Young men aged 18 to 22 joined them. Between 2023 and 2024, several members were arrested for robbery and assault. Police say these groups used WhatsApp chats to plan crimes and then carried them out while portraying themselves as mafia-style figures. “Mahakal vs Mahadev” gang rivalry A senior police officer said that on 20 May, a youth was beaten at Khapadawa crossing after members gathered through WhatsApp messages. This led to rivalry between groups. Later, two youths from the Mahadev group were shot dead. They were cousins. Nine people were arrested in the case. After getting bail, some of them tried to regroup again, though most such groups are now under police surveillance. Other gangs in different districts In Kannauj, the “Bichchu Gang” became active and was involved in violent clashes. In one incident, a youth named Arbaaz died after being beaten at a swimming pool. In Auraiya, groups like “Boss Gang” and “Mada Gang” were seen posting videos on social media with weapons. In Ballia, other groups such as “Trishul”, “Choti” and “Chingari” also operated, although most were not linked to murders. Most WhatsApp-based gangs consist of very young members. Former DGP’s view Former Uttar Pradesh DGP Sulkhan Singh said this is not new. According to him, WhatsApp is just a communication tool; the real issue is the mindset of young people who commit such crimes and try to present themselves as gangsters or mafias on social media. He said many youngsters do not understand that being a “mafioso” is not something to glorify. Why young people are turning to crime Psychologist Dr Krishna Mishra said most of these offenders are between 16 and 23 years old. He said many come from unstable family environments where conflict and antisocial behaviour are common. According to him, peer influence, show-off culture, and exposure to violence gradually push some youths towards crime as a way to fulfil their needs or gain attention.

stories.title: UPERC imposes ₹7.18 lakh fine on UPPCL:Country’s biggest penalty over delay in power restoration after smart prepaid meter recharge
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (UPERC) on Friday imposed a penalty of ₹7.18 lakh on the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL). The decision was announced by a two-member bench comprising Chairperson Arvind Kumar and member Sanjay Kumar Singh. The Commission directed that the penalty amount must be deposited within 15 days. The action was taken over negligence in not restoring electricity within two hours after the recharge of smart prepaid meters. Chaos erupted in March-April In March 2026, the electricity department converted lakhs of smart meters from postpaid to prepaid mode without obtaining consumers’ consent. As soon as the balance turned negative, electricity supply was disconnected in nearly 5 lakh households across the state. Although consumers recharged their meters, many households faced delays of up to 15 days in restoration of power. The incident triggered widespread outrage and chaos across the state. Historic decision on Consumer Council's petition The Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Consumers Council filed a petition before the Commission, alleging violation of the UPERC (Standards of Performance) Regulations, 2019. After hearing the matter, the Commission observed that the electricity department had shown serious negligence in consumer services under the smart prepaid meter system. As per regulations, power must be restored within two hours of recharge, but electricity companies failed to meet this standard. Fine of 7.18 Lakhs and Response Sought The two-member bench imposed the penalty under Sections 142 and 57 of the Electricity Act, 2003, calculating ₹1 lakh per violation along with ₹6,000 per day of delay, taking the total to ₹7.18 lakh. The Commission noted that the situation calls for a “root cause analysis” to ensure such lapses do not recur in the future. It also sought a detailed explanation from the Managing Director of UPPCL within 15 days. Demand for compensation to consumers Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Consumers Council Chairman Avadhesh Kumar Verma said this is the highest penalty ever imposed by any electricity regulatory commission in the country on a power utility, which will strengthen accountability. He further stated that a demand will soon be raised for compensation for 1.93 lakh affected consumers whose electricity was restored with a delay of more than two hours after recharge.

stories.title: Yogi Govt to fill 38,000 jobs in 4 months:10,000 more recruitments likely before elections; youth outreach ahead of polls
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Yogi Adityanath government has stepped up efforts to woo young voters. The state is preparing to create a favourable political atmosphere by completing the recruitment process for more than 38,000 posts across various departments through the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC). The commission has already completed examinations and interviews for 23,668 posts in 115 departments by March 2026. Dates have also been finalised for examinations and interviews for 10,445 posts in 48 departments between June and September. In addition, application forms are currently being accepted for recruitment to 3,685 posts in several departments. Recruitment notifications for nearly 10,000 more posts are also expected to be announced in the coming days. Recruitments increased after poor Lok Sabha election results The pace of these recruitments, mainly for Group C posts, increased significantly after the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Before the polls, many government departments were not sending proposals for vacant posts to the commission. After the election results fell short of expectations, a review reportedly found that unemployment and paper leaks were among the biggest reasons for youth dissatisfaction. Following this, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed all departments to immediately send proposals for filling vacant positions. As a result of this push, departments have been continuously forwarding proposals, and the government is now aiming to fill these 38,000 posts before the elections to strengthen its support among young voters. Preparation to woo youth through employment Senior journalist Anand Rai believes the government is trying to connect with young voters through its employment mission. According to him, efforts are being made to counter the narrative built by the Opposition after the Lok Sabha elections. He pointed out that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has been holding appointment-letter distribution ceremonies every month, while the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission, UPSSSC, Education Service Selection Commission and Police Recruitment Board continue to release vacancies. 9 lakh government recruitments never happened before Senior journalist Virendranath Bhatt says no government in the last 20 years has carried out recruitment on such a scale. The Yogi government claims to have recruited around 900,000 people in nine years. Recruitments for nearly 150,000 posts are currently underway through various recruitment bodies. Filling vacant government posts not only improves administrative functioning but also helps create a positive political atmosphere for the ruling party by generating employment opportunities. Completing recruitment on time is a challenge for the commission Experts say the commission has begun releasing recruitment notifications regularly after a long gap. On June 2, it released its examination and interview calendar. However, conducting examinations and interviews on time and declaring results promptly remains a major challenge for the commission. One reason is the shortage of staff. Five of the eight member positions in the commission are currently vacant. As a result, interviews often take longer to complete. A lack of employees also delays document verification. Ensuring that recruitment processes are not stalled due to legal challenges in the High Court and Supreme Court will be another significant test for the commission.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Fire breaks out in a 28-storey Noida apartment; India's GDP falls to 3-quarter low of 7.8% in Q4 more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. India's GDP falls to 3-quarter low of 7.8% in Q4 India’s GDP growth slowed to a three-quarter low of 7.8% in the March quarter of FY26, mainly due to weaker agriculture and manufacturing performance. However, the government raised full-year growth estimates to 7.7% on stronger consumer spending, while introducing a new 2022-23 base year for GDP calculations. 2. Fire breaks out in a 28-storey Noida apartment, residents safely evacuated A fire broke out in a 28-storey Ivy County Society tower in Noida’s Sector 75 after a suspected AC short circuit on the 12th floor. Residents were safely evacuated as fire teams used cranes to control the blaze. No casualties reported so far. 3. Bulldozer demolishes illegal ‘Mazar’ in Sambhal amid heavy security deployment Authorities in Sambhal demolished a mazar built on government land, citing illegal encroachment after court orders. Police said the structure was removed following legal proceedings, while the caretaker claimed it was a centuries-old shrine and disputed the administration’s timeline and ownership findings. 4. Annamalai quits BJP, to launch new ‘political movement’ Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamalai has launched a new political party after quitting the BJP, citing ideological differences with the leadership. The former IPS officer said he informed the party of his decision in December 2025 and plans to contest the 2031 Assembly elections. 5. Ghazipur SP warns strict action against miscreants; DIG conducts night flag march Tension erupted in Ghazipur after an encounter killing of accused Kamlesh Bind, leading to stone-pelting on police and injuries to officers. DIG conducted a midnight flag march, while SP warned of strict action and FIRs were filed against several named and unidentified persons involved in violence. 6. Haryanvi dancer Dimple Chaudhary slaps man during Hathras stage show after harassment Haryanvi dancer Dimple Chaudhary slapped a man during a stage show in Hathras after he allegedly touched her inappropriately. She condemned the act on stage, saying performers must be respected. The incident created chaos, but no police complaint was filed by the artist. 7. Putin says US pressure on Modi is futile Russia has offered India joint development and production of the Su-57 stealth fighter jet, with President Vladimir Putin saying Moscow is ready to share advanced defence technologies. Putin also said external pressure on India would be ineffective, praised Prime Minister Modi’s leadership, and expressed confidence that India-Russia trade will reach $100 billion in the coming years. 8. Trailer hits motorcycle in Gorakhpur, husband-wife killed, son seriously injured A husband and wife were killed after their motorcycle was hit by a trailer truck in Chauri Chaura, Gorakhpur. Their seven-year-old son was seriously injured and hospitalised. The trailer driver fled the spot after the accident. Police have launched an investigation and initiated legal proceedings. 9. Reporter exposes alleged UP conversion network through undercover labourer operation A journalist exposed an alleged religious conversion network in Uttar Pradesh by going undercover as a labourer. The report claims people were persuaded to abandon Hindu practices, including removing sacred threads, through emotional and faith-based influence, with promises of relief from personal and financial hardships. 10. Shreyas Iyer to become India's T20I skipper Shreyas Iyer is reportedly set to become India’s new T20 captain, replacing Suryakumar Yadav, who has been removed from the role. Tilak Varma is likely to be appointed vice-captain, while 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is expected to earn a maiden senior team call-up after a standout IPL season.

stories.title: Bulldozer razes mazar in Sambhal:70 security personnel deployed, SP vows removal of illegal structures
stories.summary: A shrine (mazar) was demolished by the administration in Uttar Pradesh's Sambhal district on Friday, with officials claiming it had been built illegally on government land around 4-5 years ago. However, the shrine's caretaker, Aziz, said the Pir Baba shrine was 500-600 years old. The administration arrived at the site in Baghau village under the Gunnaur police station area, about 29 km from the district headquarters, with two bulldozers on Friday morning. The structure was demolished within an hour. Superintendent of Police (SP) KK Bishnoi and District Magistrate (DM) Ankit Khandelwal were present during the operation. The shrine was located in the catchment area of the Mahawa river. Officials said the Tehsil Court had ordered the demolition of the shrine. The caretaker later challenged the order in the DM Court, but the appeal was also rejected. Following the court rulings, the administration carried out the demolition drive. Around 70 personnel from the Gunnaur police and the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) were deployed to maintain law and order. SP KK Bishnoi said the demolished structure was a religious building situated on government land. "We are freeing government land from illegal construction and encroachment in Sambhal to create a land bank. So far, more than 100 hectares of land have been cleared," he said. First see 3 pictures Now understand the entire matter in a sequential manner- In Baghau village, there was a religious structure named 'Khere Wale Baba Chaman Shah Baba Dargah Sharif Mazar'. According to the Lekhpal's investigation report, illegal possession by Aziz son of Allan, resident of Baghau, was found on 24 square meters of land from Gata number 592. A case was filed by Gram Sabha Baghau against Aziz under Section 67 of UP Revenue Code 2006 on April 18, 2026. The investigation revealed that the construction was done after taking possession in the name of 'Ziyarat' about 5 years ago. After the hearing, the Tehsildar court ordered removal of encroachment, payment of Rs 39 thousand as compensation and Rs 300 as execution fee. Aziz challenged the order in the District Magistrate's court. On June 3, 2026, the court dismissed the petition. After this, the administration expedited the process of removing illegal construction. Tehsildar Ravi Sonkar formed a special team. Naib Tehsildar Anuj Kumar was made the team in-charge. Along with officers and employees of the revenue department, 70 police personnel including personnel from Babrala police station, Gunnour police, and PAC were deployed for security. See pictures of the shrine before bulldozer action- Claim- 500-600 year old mazar in the name of Pir Baba Mutawalli Aziz said that there is a 500-600 year old shrine known as Pir Baba. Many generations have changed. You can inquire in the surrounding villages, there were only two things here - Mata Rani and Pir Baba. Many people come here, those who come for darshan of Mata Rani also visit the shrine. They demolished the front shrine. We had no problem even then. The administration broke the gate, even then we did nothing. DM said - encroachment was found in investigation DM Ankit Khandelwal informed- This case was related to encroachment on public land. A case was filed in the Tehsildar's court under Section 67 and a hearing was conducted, in which encroachment was found. After hearing all parties and examining evidence, the appeal was dismissed. When no concrete evidence was found in favor of possession, action was taken to remove the encroachment.

stories.title: Ghazipur SP warns of tough action against miscreants:DIG conducts midnight flag march, FIR filed against 5
stories.summary: Tension gripped Ghazipur after the police encounter killing of murder accused Kamlesh Bind. A crowd allegedly pelted stones at police personnel, leaving several officers, including a Circle Officer (CO) and Station House Officer (SHO), injured. The violence continued for nearly 40 minutes. Police teams from multiple stations and personnel from the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) were deployed to bring the situation under control. The area was subsequently placed under heavy security. DIG conducts midnight inspection Vaibhav Krishna, DIG of Varanasi Range, reached the site around midnight. He conducted a flag march using torches in the dark, inspected the scene and reviewed the situation with officials. Police have so far registered a case against six named individuals, including Kamlesh's brother and sister-in-law, along with 40 to 50 unidentified persons. SP warns of strict action Superintendent of Police Eraj Raja also visited the scene and issued a stern warning. He said- Those involved in violence will be dealt with strictly. Every individual who pelted stones at the police will face the strongest possible action. The National Security Act (NSA) will also be invoked where necessary. Murder of hotelier’s son On the night of May 29, four assailants allegedly shot dead Vineet Rai, son of hotelier Alok Rai, in Ghazipur. Alok Rai subsequently named Katra Gang leader Shankar Pandey, Sonu Yadav, Kamlesh Bind and Monu Tripathi in the FIR. Meanwhile, a non-bailable warrant (NBW) has been issued against Shankar Pandey. The Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) court has directed Ghazipur Police to produce him before the court by June 25. The warrant, however, relates to a separate five-year-old student murder case. Pictures of protest-stone pelting- Know the incident in five key points 1. Kamlesh Bind killed in encounter On the night of June 3, police shot dead Kamlesh Bind, a resident of Goda village (Sohilapur), during an encounter. A reward of ₹1 lakh had been announced for his arrest. The remaining accused in the Vineet Rai murder case, Shankar Pandey, Sonu Yadav and Monu Tripathi, remain absconding. Police have announced rewards of- 2. Protest erupts during funeral procession At around 7 pm, family members took Kamlesh's body for cremation at a site approximately five kilometres from the village. Women from the family initially carried the bier before the body was placed in a pickup vehicle. Police personnel accompanied the procession. After travelling around 500 metres, protesters stopped near the Phullanpur railway crossing and placed the body on the road. The crowd then began accusing police of staging a fake encounter. 3. Stone-pelting begins Eyewitnesses said police attempted to calm the protesters, leading to a confrontation. The situation escalated from pushing and shoving to large-scale stone-pelting. Stones were allegedly thrown from multiple directions, forcing police personnel to seek cover. Some officers reportedly took shelter inside a nearby bank building. 4. Several policemen injured Among those injured were- CO Sengar’s driver, Shashikant Pandey, also sustained injuries to his shoulder and back, while his wristwatch was damaged during the incident. 5. Cremation conducted under police security After dispersing the crowd, police took custody of the body and transported it to the cremation ground. Kamlesh’s elder brother, Sanjay Kumar Bind, lit the funeral pyre. Witnesses said he broke down in tears during the final rites. Only eight to ten people were present at the cremation. Kamlesh got married just 36 days earlier Kamlesh Bind married Manisha, a resident of Mohania in Bihar, on April 27, only 36 days before the encounter. Manisha is a nursing student. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, she alleged- My husband was innocent. Police forcibly picked him up from Rampur. On May 30, they kept me and my sister-in-law at the police station. I saw officers beating him there before taking him away. Kamlesh’s elder brother Sanjay Kumar Bind also claimed the encounter was fake and alleged his brother had been falsely implicated. He further accused hotel owner Alok Rai of framing Kamlesh over disputes linked to activities allegedly taking place at the hotel. Non-bailable warrant issued against Shankar Pandey Assistant Government Advocate Akhilesh Singh said a student murder case dating back to 2021 was scheduled for hearing on Thursday. According to the prosecution, the student was lured to a shrine and murdered. Shankar Pandey is the principal accused in that case. When neither Shankar nor his lawyer appeared in court, the prosecution informed CJM Shakti Singh that the accused was also wanted in another murder case. The court subsequently issued a non-bailable warrant. Who Is Shankar Pandey? According to police, Shankar Pandey is a notorious criminal who heads the Katra Gang. Officials claim the gang is involved in extortion, criminal intimidation robbery and violent attacks. Police allege the gang operates through a WhatsApp group where instructions are circulated before crimes are carried out. Hotelier Alok Rai claimed Shankar Pandey had been demanding extortion money for the past two years. According to Rai- He used to say the hotel was worth ₹20 crore and demanded ₹1 crore in protection money. He also alleged that the gang vandalised the hotel on several occasions. Members of the group reportedly referred to themselves on social media as the “King of Ghazipur”, while Shankar described himself as a “Bahubali” (strongman). Major cases linked to the gang According to allegations cited by Alok Rai- September 5, 2024: Textile trader Sachin Chaurasia abducted and subjected to an attempted murder attack. November 26, 2024: Photographer Vipin Chaurasia chased and assaulted in a marketplace. December 12, 2025: Vaibhav Singh attacked and severely beaten. May 9, 2026: Shubham Chaubey shot in broad daylight at Jhunnulal Chowk. How Vineet Rai was killed Vineet Rai, 29, son of hotelier Alok Rai, was shot dead during the night of May 29–30. According to investigators, four masked assailants arrived on two motorcycles pretending to purchase beer. The attack took place at around 4 am as Vineet was preparing to leave the hotel for home. As he approached his car, the attackers allegedly opened fire using two pistols. Police said Vineet suffered- The attackers also allegedly chased a security guard, who managed to escape. After firing into the air, the assailants fled the scene. Vineet was taken to a medical college hospital, where he later died during treatment. Police version of the encounter According to SP Eraj Raja, police teams had been conducting continuous raids in search of the accused. At around 9 pm on June 3, officers received information that Kamlesh Bind was hiding near Pavhari Baba Ashram in Kurtha. Police and SWAT teams cordoned off the area. Officials said a man riding a motorcycle without a registration plate was spotted approaching. When officers attempted to stop him, he allegedly opened fire from a distance of around 800 metres. Police returned fire, injuring the suspect. Upon approaching him, officers identified him as Kamlesh Bind. He was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police said they recovered- According to police records, Kamlesh had seven criminal cases registered against him, including charges related to murder, attempted murder, kidnapping, assault, criminal intimidation and violations of the Arms Act. His first criminal case was registered in 2017.

stories.title: Ramgarhtal water to be cleaned in Gorakhpur:GDA launches restoration drive following Chief Minister Yogi's Directive
stories.summary: An initiative to clean the water of Ramgarhtal, a popular picnic destination for residents of Gorakhpur and neighbouring districts, has been launched. While inaugurating a picnic spot developed on the banks of Chilua Tal, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath compared the water quality of the two lakes. He described Chilua Tal as cleaner and more natural. While appreciating the efforts already made to improve the condition of Ramgarhtal, the Chief Minister directed officials to ensure that the lake is completely cleaned. Following the directive, the Gorakhpur Development Authority (GDA) has initiated the process. Vice-Chairman Abhinav Gopal is overseeing the preparation of a detailed action plan. Applications from interested firms will soon be invited. Officials say a substantial quantity of silt will need to be removed before the lake's water can be fully restored. Water levels falling during summer Water levels in Ramgarhtal have begun to decline due to the summer season. However, officials said the lake still maintains a depth of more than four metres. To ensure adequate water levels are maintained, drainage from the lake will be restricted. During the monsoon season, the lake generally receives sufficient inflow to replenish water levels. Silt and foul smell identified as major challenges The largest challenge facing Ramgarhtal is the accumulation of silt, estimated at more than 80 lakh cubic metres. Extensive desilting will be required to restore the lake. Residents are also affected by a recurring foul smell emanating from the water. The agency selected for the project will be tasked with preparing a comprehensive plan to address issues including- Detailed survey to be conducted first Under the authority’s proposed plan, a detailed survey of Ramgarhtal will be carried out before restoration work begins. The survey will include- The study will also determine the causes of- Modern technologies to be evaluated Several modern and scientific techniques will be considered to improve water quality. For odour control, authorities will evaluate options including- Focus On desilting and pollution control To tackle accumulated silt, the plan will explore the use of- These measures are intended to improve water quality and maintain clarity in the lake. Measures planned to prevent future pollution Keeping Ramgarhtal's catchment area in mind, the restoration plan will also include- Officials say these measures are aimed at preventing pollution from recurring in the future. Agencies to submit long-term management plans According to Kishan Singh, Chief Engineer of the Authority, participating agencies will be required to present detailed proposals covering- Regular monitoring of water quality, odour reduction and silt management standards will also be carried out. GDA to invite applications soon GDA Vice-Chairman Abhinav Gopal said a comprehensive plan has been prepared to further improve Ramgarhtal. He said interested firms will soon be invited to participate through an Expression of Interest (EOI) process. According to Gopal, the objective is to make the lake completely clean and restore its ecological health.

stories.title: Haryanvi dancer slaps man during stage show in Hathras:Dimple Chaudhary got furious after he touched her waist
stories.summary: Haryanvi stage dancer Dimple Chaudhary was subjected to inappropriate behaviour during a stage performance in Hathras, Uttar Pradesh. Dimple also shared a video of the incident on her Instagram account. In the footage, a young man can be seen touching her waist while she was performing on stage. Angered by the act, Dimple slapped the man on stage and later reprimanded him using the microphone, saying- Just because a performance is going on doesn't mean you can touch me. Dimple Chaudhary is originally from Bulandshahr in Uttar Pradesh and regularly performs stage shows across Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Following the incident, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to her about what happened. Some PHOTOS of the dispute with the Haryanvi dancer on stage ‘Several artists were performing at the event’ Dimple said the incident took place on June 3 in the Hathras area of Uttar Pradesh. According to her, a dance and Ragini programme had been organised to celebrate a man's daughter's birthday. The event began at around 8 pm, while she went on stage at approximately 10 pm. She said several performers, including dancers and singers Shivani, Komal Chaudhary and other artists, were taking turns to perform throughout the evening. Dimple said that at around 2.30 am, she was performing to the Haryanvi song Gandass when a young man climbed onto the stage. She alleged that the man, who was a relative of the organiser, attempted to touch her waist inappropriately during the performance. She said she immediately reacted by slapping him on stage. Speaking about the incident, Dimple said performers work on stage both to entertain audiences and to earn a livelihood. She added that this does not give anyone the right to violate their dignity. If anyone tries to behave inappropriately or harass us with wrong intentions, it will not be tolerated. She also acknowledged that, in the heat of the moment, she used some harsh language while confronting the man. No police complaint filed When asked whether she would pursue legal action, Dimple said she had already responded to the man's behaviour on the spot and therefore did not wish to file a police complaint. She added that the incident caused considerable commotion at the venue and that sticks had to be used to control the crowd after tensions escalated. Dimple began her career in 2018 Dimple Chaudhary said she began working as a stage performer in 2018. She explained that her family's financial condition was difficult, which led her to choose performing as a career. Initially, her family opposed the decision, but later supported her after seeing her dedication and success. She also said she completed her Class 12 education during the Covid period. Started by singing at Jagrans Dimple said she began her career singing bhajans and devotional songs at jagrans. She later moved into stage performances and gradually built a reputation in the regional dance circuit. According to her, she initially earned only ₹500 per programme. Today, she charges up to ₹40,000 for a two-hour stage show. Responding to criticism over dance performances and the use of strong language on social media, Dimple said- This is my livelihood and how I support my family. People enjoy my performances, which is why they invite me. Those who don't like them are free to leave. She added that she performs regularly in Haryana and attracts large crowds at her shows.

stories.summary: A massive fire broke out on Friday morning at around 8 am in a high-rise residential society in Noida’s Sector 74. The blaze erupted in a flat located on the 12th floor of a 28-storey building. The fire spread rapidly, and within moments, flames began shooting out from the flat’s windows. Thick black smoke spread into the sky and filled the entire society. Panic as residents rush To evacuate Panic gripped the residential complex as residents rushed out in chaos. People ran down the staircases to escape the building. On receiving information, multiple fire brigade vehicles and police teams reached the spot. Efforts were launched to bring the fire under control. The building was evacuated, and as a precaution, residents of nearby flats were also moved to safe locations. Hydraulic crane deployed to control blaze Initially, the water pressure from the fire engines could reach only up to the 6th floor, while the fire was on the 12th floor. After some time, a hydraulic crane was brought in, and water was then directed into the affected flat. The situation improved as the building was equipped with fire safety systems, which helped control the blaze after nearly two and a half hours of effort. As a precaution, nearby towers were also evacuated. No casualties have been reported so far. When fire brigade water failed to reach the 12th floor, a resident remarked: “Is this a fire brigade or a Holi fountain? Water is not reaching above 6–7 floors. This is our infrastructure. They are just watering plants in the houses below. It’s a useless system.” Meanwhile, another fire incident was reported in Noida. A fire broke out at a paying guest (PG) accommodation in the ‘E-3 Shatabdi Vihar’ area of Sector-52. The building has a restaurant on the ground floor and PG accommodation for students on the upper floors. The fire started in a refrigerator at the restaurant due to a short circuit. Fifteen people trapped inside were safely evacuated, and the fire was brought under control. See 5 photos - Fire safety arrangements in high-rise buildings in Noida In Noida, fire services are equipped with hydraulic platforms and articulating water towers for firefighting in high-rise buildings and societies. These machines range from 30 to 42 metres and can reach up to around 10 floors. Additionally, 72-metre and 102-metre hydraulic systems are being procured but are not yet available. The tallest building in Noida is Supernova in Sector-94, planned as an 80-storey tower, with 60 floors already completed and occupied. However, only four hydraulic units are available there, capable of reaching up to 42 metres. An air-compressed foam system was tested there earlier, which can reach up to 300 metres, but it is not yet in operational use. Firefighting operations highlighted the challenges of tackling blazes in high-rise buildings, especially where access and water pressure limitations delay response at upper floors. While rapid evacuation and timely deployment of fire tenders helped prevent casualties in both incidents, the events once again underscored gaps in high-rise fire response infrastructure and the need for stronger emergency preparedness systems in rapidly growing urban residential clusters.

stories.title: Rain lashes Lucknow, Agra and three other cities:Alert issued for 38 districts; IMD warns of storms within three hours
stories.summary: Stormy and rainy conditions continue across Uttar Pradesh. Strong winds have been sweeping through Lucknow since Friday morning, accompanied by light rain, thunderclouds and occasional lightning. Cloud cover has also been reported in more than 10 cities. Drizzle was recorded in Barabanki, Bahraich, Agra and Bareilly. Meanwhile, the Meteorological Department has issued a thunderstorm alert for Lucknow and the surrounding areas for the next three hours. According to mobile alerts sent to residents, wind speeds could range between 40 and 70 kmph, with light to moderate rainfall also likely. Rain and thunderstorm alert in 38 districts A rain and thunderstorm alert has been issued for 38 districts across the state today. Of these, 21 districts are under an orange alert, while 17 districts have been placed under a yellow alert. The Meteorological Department said a Western Disturbance will remain active over the state for the next 24 hours, leading to continued thunderstorms and rainfall. After that, weather conditions are expected to change, with temperatures rising again and summer heat intensifying. Gorakhpur records highest rainfall On Thursday, the impact of the Western Disturbance was felt across several districts in both eastern and western UP. Rain accompanied by strong winds was reported in many areas. Gorakhpur recorded the highest rainfall at 21.7 mm. Light showers were also reported in Barabanki, Sitapur, Prayagraj, Meerut and Aligarh, among other districts. Banda remained the hottest city in the state, recording a maximum temperature of 42.2°C. Atul Kumar Singh, Senior Scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre in Lucknow, said- Due to the impact of the new Western Disturbance, there is a continued possibility of thunderstorms, strong winds and scattered light rainfall across Uttar Pradesh. The system is expected to weaken within the next one or two days. After that, severe heat will return and continue until the arrival of the monsoon. The monsoon is expected to enter the state through Gorakhpur by June 18 and may reach Lucknow by June 22. Weather forecast for the next four days June 6- Light rainfall is expected in most districts. Moisture levels in the air will remain high, keeping temperatures largely stable. Heatwave conditions are not expected. June 7- Light rain is likely across the state. Periods of bright sunshine between showers could increase humidity levels and make conditions uncomfortable. June 8- The weather is expected to remain clear across Uttar Pradesh. Strong sunshine is forecast, and there is no possibility of rainfall. June 9- Most districts are likely to experience bright sunshine. Winds of up to 30 kmph may provide some relief from humid conditions.

stories.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on 3-Day visit to Lucknow:Will go to Aparna Yadav’s Residence, plant saplings on Environment Day, and interact with residents
stories.summary: Union Defence Minister and Lucknow MP Rajnath Singh will be on a three-day visit to the state capital from June 5 to 7. During the visit, he will attend a series of social, religious and organisational programmes, meet residents in different parts of the city, and participate in interaction sessions with prominent citizens and party functionaries. According to BJP Metropolitan President Anand Dwivedi, Rajnath Singh will arrive at Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport at 11.05 am on Friday. Following his arrival, he will visit the homes of the late Ashok Motiyani in Hind Nagar, the late Darshan Lal in Krishna Nagar, and Rupa Devi in Badi Lal Kurti in the Cantonment area to meet their families and offer condolences. To plant saplings under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign At 12.15 pm, the Defence Minister will plant saplings at Kasturba Park as part of the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ (One Tree in Mother’s Name) campaign. He will then visit the residence of Aparna Yadav before proceeding to his residence on Kalidas Marg. To attend Ram Katha Mahotsav At 4 pm, Rajnath Singh will take part in the ‘Bioyug Green Command’ programme at Dilkusha Lawn. Later, at 5.25 pm, he will attend the Ram Katha Mahotsav at the Seva Hospital complex on Sitapur Road, where he will participate in a religious discourse being delivered by Jagadguru Rambhadracharya. Dialogue programmes scheduled for June 6 And 7 On June 6, Rajnath Singh will meet several families in Gomtinagar and Nirala Nagar. In the evening, he will participate in an interaction programme with prominent citizens from Paschim Mandal-2 at Millennium Palace on Hardoi Road. On June 7, he will attend another interaction session with distinguished citizens and community representatives of Cantt Mandal-1 at GP Hotel Banquet in Alambagh before departing for New Delhi.

stories.title: Monsoon to reach UP by June 24:Expected to cover state in 10 days, may weaken after 20–25 days
stories.summary: Monsoon is expected to reach Uttar Pradesh by June 24 this year. Once it arrives, it is likely to cover the entire state within 10 days. Normally, the monsoon enters UP between June 18 and 20, making it around four days late this year. Weather experts also expect the monsoon to weaken after 20–25 days. A fresh Western Disturbance became active over the state on June 4, bringing rain and thunderstorms until June 7. After that, the system is expected to weaken, allowing temperatures to rise again. The monsoon entered India through Kerala on June 4, four days later than usual. Monsoon likely to enter through Purvanchal, not Bundelkhand The Meteorological Department estimates that the monsoon will enter UP from the eastern region in 2026. A similar pattern was seen in 2023. In the following two years, however, the monsoon entered through Bundelkhand. Previous monsoon entry routes 2023- The monsoon entered UP on June 24 via Bihar, affecting eastern districts including Ballia and Deoria. 2024- The monsoon arrived on June 25 through Lalitpur and Jhansi and covered the entire state by June 30. 2025- The monsoon reached UP on June 18. Initial rainfall was recorded in Sonbhadra, Jhansi and Lalitpur, all part of the Bundelkhand region. Rain and thunderstorms first, then temperatures to rise The combination of a Western Disturbance and moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal will continue to influence weather conditions across UP in June. The Meteorological Department has issued a yellow alert for rain and thunderstorms across the state on June 5 and 6. After June 7, the Western Disturbance is expected to weaken. Between June 7 and 9, temperatures are likely to rise again, with heatwave-like conditions returning to some districts. Due to the impact of El Niño, intermittent hot winds may continue through June. Weather outlook for Western and Eastern UP 1. Western UP The Western Disturbance will have a stronger impact on western districts. Areas such as Meerut, Noida, Ghaziabad, Baghpat, Saharanpur and Aligarh are likely to witness thunderstorms, lightning and strong winds. Wind speeds may reach 70–80 kmph, bringing a fall of 2–4°C in daytime temperatures and providing temporary relief from the heat. However, from June 7 onwards, intense sunshine and dry winds from Rajasthan could push temperatures back up to 44–47°C. Heatwave conditions may return to districts including Meerut, Agra, Aligarh and Noida. The peak of the heat is expected around mid-June. Western UP is likely to receive the monsoon last, either in the final week of June or in early July. 2. Eastern UP The impact of the Western Disturbance will be less pronounced in Purvanchal. Cloud cover is expected in districts such as Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Ballia and Deoria. Only isolated areas are likely to receive light showers, thunderstorms or lightning activity. Moist winds from the Bay of Bengal are expected to increase humidity levels significantly. Temperatures will not fall substantially, resulting in uncomfortable and sticky conditions. Winds are likely to blow at speeds of 40–50 kmph. Weather conditions in eastern UP will differ from those in the west due to the influence of Bay of Bengal winds. From the second week of June onwards, humid and hot conditions are expected to intensify in districts including Prayagraj, Varanasi, Gorakhpur and Ballia. As the monsoon is expected to reach eastern UP between June 24 and 29, rainfall activity is likely to begin after June 22. UP may receive 8% less rainfall Senior scientist Atul Singh said rainfall across the country, including Uttar Pradesh, is expected to remain below normal this year. Typically, UP receives around 820–840 mm of rainfall between June and September. This year, rainfall is projected to be 8% below normal, amounting to approximately 754–773 mm. Impact on agriculture, inflation may rise Reduced rainfall due to El Niño could have a direct impact on the state's economy, agriculture and daily life. Paddy production may decline by up to 20%. A lack of rainfall during June and July could delay paddy transplantation and reduce the total cultivated area. Farmers may have to rely more heavily on tube wells for irrigation. Higher electricity and diesel costs could significantly increase farming expenses. Lower agricultural output could push up the prices of cereals, pulses and vegetables. There are also concerns that drought conditions could intensify in Bundelkhand and south-western UP districts, including Jhansi, Mahoba, Lalitpur and Mathura.

stories.title: Sacred thread cut off from hand, stopped from worshipping:Reporter goes undercover as labourer to expose UP conversion network
stories.summary: “If you want Jesus’ prayer to have an effect, you must remove the sacred thread tied around your wrist. Otherwise, your troubles will never go away. And yes, stay away from worship.” This was said to a Dainik Bhaskar reporter during an alleged brainwashing session aimed at religious conversion. In Uttar Pradesh, people are allegedly being persuaded to change their faith with promises of relief from illness, poverty and personal hardships. Dainik Bhaskar received information about secret churches operating in Lakhimpur district. These centres reportedly have no signboards and display no images of Jesus. To avoid attracting police attention, the process is no longer referred to as conversion; instead, organisers call it “Grahan” (acceptance). To expose what is claimed to be a large-scale conversion network operating along the India-Nepal border, the Dainik Bhaskar team went undercover. The reporters disguised themselves as labourers and worked in fields for 20 days. During this period, the group made contact with them. Hidden-camera recordings allegedly revealed multiple layers of the network. Seven stages of conversion revealed When the reporter entered the alleged conversion network, seven stages of the process emerged. In Part 1 of this investigation, we explain the first three stages. Stage 1: Winning trust through local contacts The team reached Dalrajpur village in Lakhimpur district disguised as labourers. They searched for work within a 4-km radius and eventually found employment at a farmhouse. A hut was provided for accommodation. While working there, they gradually built relationships with local residents. The reporters spoke about their supposed hardships, claiming they were poor and suffering from illness. Before long, this information allegedly reached Pastor Vijay, a Christian cleric originally from Nepal. According to locals, he has been active in the area for around 30 years and operates a secret church from his home. His associates allegedly identify poor and sick individuals and encourage them to visit him. On the tenth day, a group of labourers advised the reporters to meet Pastor Vijay. A visit to his secret church was arranged for Sunday morning at 8 am. Stage 2: Emotional persuasion through personal testimonies The reporters arrived at the church at the appointed time. Pastor Vijay seated them beside him and remained silent for a while before beginning a conversation. Pastor Vijay- So, what is your problem? Reporter- We work at the farmhouse. Problems keep coming one after another. Our whole family has suffered because of them. I cannot get rid of my addiction. My left hand does not lift properly. We never manage to save any money. We even had to sell our land. Pastor Vijay- You have come to the place where the path opens. The Lord says in His word that whoever comes near Him, He comes near them. The Lord stays close to those whose lives are full of troubles. To reinforce the message, Pastor Vijay called over two more people, government school teacher Shivprasad Gautam and his wife. Pastor Vijay- This is our teacher. For two to four years, his life was full of difficulties. He wasted ₹12–13 lakh because of his problems. Whatever he earned from his job went into that. Then he came closer to the Lord, and all those problems disappeared. Pastor Vijay then showed passages from his mobile phone. Government Teacher Shivprasad Gautam- You have come to the right place because we wander only as much as is written in our destiny. Pastor Vijay- You do not need to worry. If you have any problem, we can even pray for you over the phone. Reporter- Will I need to come here again? Pastor Vijay- Yes, you will have to come once or twice more. Shivprasad’s Wife- Do not worry. You will recover. Consider yourself to be sitting in God’s house.” Reporter- Okay. Shivprasad’s Wife- A Baba is coming from Nepal. It would be good if he listens to your problem. It may take him some time to arrive. You are not in a hurry, are you? Reporter- No. Pastor Vijay- Come and sit closer to us. He then placed his hand on the reporter’s head and asked him to repeat a prayer. Pastor Vijay- Repeat after me: Lord, we come to your refuge. I surrender my life to you. Reporter- Lord, we come to your refuge. I surrender my life to you. Stage 3: Asking followers to abandon Hindu symbols and practices Once the group appeared satisfied that the reporter had accepted their message, they moved to the next stage. The reporter was told that Jesus’ prayers would not work unless Hindu religious symbols and practices were abandoned. Shivprasad’s Wife- You have not worn any amulets or anything, have you? Reporter- A worship ceremony was performed about a month ago. That is when this sacred thread was tied. Shivprasad’s Wife- If you remove this thread, the prayers we offer will reach you. Otherwise, it will cause harm. It is linked to ritual practices. Please remove it. We also used to observe fasts. When prayers were offered for us, they would not reach us. Pastor Vijay- (Pointing towards Shivprasad) He once told me there was nothing left in his house. But my Lord told me there was still a lot there. We went to his house and started opening cupboards and storage spaces. Things kept emerging. Shivprasad’s Wife- There was also water kept there. What kind of water was it? Was it from Haridwar? Reporter- Do you mean Ganga water from Haridwar or Prayagraj? Shivprasad’s Wife- Yes. That water was blocking the prayer. Pastor Vijay- Our objective is that prayer should not stop anywhere. If it connects, it should connect completely. Shivprasad’s Wife- (To the pastor) Weren’t you noticing? While praying, he was making ‘foen-foen’ sounds. The prayer was becoming ineffective. Pastor Vijay- He was under a very dangerous influence. Even petrol and diesel could not burn the ‘jantu’. Reporter- What is a ‘jantu’? Others Present- Amulets and such things. Pastor Vijay- In our language, we call all these things ‘jantu’. During the conversation, someone brought a blade. Pastor Vijay then cut the sacred thread from the reporter’s wrist and said they would keep it. What has the investigation revealed so far? According to the findings of the undercover investigation-
